posts.text: For MSTC, the CPCB EPRETP guidelines document (January 2025) plus the E-Waste Management Rules 2022 as amended, plus the price band notifications under each waste-category rule, plus the CPCB tender document that awarded MSTC the platform, together contain almost all the information needed to size the EPR opportunity correctly. Management concalls add color but do not add ground truth. The CPCB guidelines document is the actual governing regulation. posts.text: Can you substantiate with detailed proof from various concalls/. ground data ? For example this is Namo-ewaste ‘s data on “just” e-waste . Numbers might be inflated , but If i do a sum of parts of ~ 15 industries where EPR is getting mandated , roughly 34K Cr is not very hard to achieve . Also the EPR rates that we are quoting is the minimum rate and as far as I understand government wants the rates to be market driven . image 1920×1076 552 KB Very nice article on the EPR theme : How India's E-waste rules found their teeth?
